newsitem.title: LEBANON: Syria says it wants good relations with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Syria says it wants good relations with Turkey.

text.p: Syria on Thursday denied Turkish charges that it helped Kurdish separatists fighting Ankara and said Turkish-Israeli military cooperation was directed against Arab interests.

Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam told reporters after meeting Lebanese leaders that Damascus wanted good relations with Turkey and there was no question of breaking diplomatic relations with Ankara.
Replying to questions, he said Turkey's military incursion into northern Iraq against anti-Turkish Kurds was a matter of concern for all Arab countries.
"The Israeli-Turkish partnership is an economic, political and security-related one that aims at controlling the region, hitting Arab interests," Khaddam added.

"We all have to work on convincing Turkey to review this policy which in both the short and long term is not for the good of Turkey and does not contribute to peace and stability in the region," he said.
Asked whether the Turkish-Israeli alliance could bring war to the region, Khaddam said: "We don't want or expect or conclude this. We hope no one miscalculates."
He said Syrian and Iraqi trade delegations were visiting each other's countries in an effort to help ease the sufferings of the Iraqi people caused by a U.N. embargo, but these had no political role.
"We have not spoken of a political dimension of the role of these delegations," Khaddam said.

Khaddam and Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara were in Beirut to brief Lebanese President Elias Hrawi, Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and Foreign Minister Faris Bouez on the results of their tour of Arab capitals.
Asked if Syria was helping Kurdish separatist insurgents against Turkey, Khaddam said Turkey sometimes made baseless accusations against his country as a result of internal Turkish circumstances.

"But the Turkish government...has nothing proving that any assistance goes from Syria to the PKK," Khaddam said, referring to Turkey's Kurdistan Workers Party which is fighting Ankara for Kurdish autonomy or independence.
"We want good neighbourly relations with Turkey and other Islamist countries like Iran. What would Syria benefit from a state of instability in Turkey? Nothing at all," he said.
